$ADC $FBIOP This is trading at a 36% discount to its $25 par value. I understand why there is a discount, given the interest rate environment in the US relative to the original 4.25% annual coupon rate; however, this discount will not last forever, so in the long run, one should be able to count on some price appreciation. In the meantime, this preferred stock offers the most secure monthly dividend I have ever seen.

$ADC  Not to brag, but I have a friend in the US (he’s actually my only friend in the US...), and he works for this company and has nothing but good things to say. He understands why insiders have been buying millions’ worth of shares lately, even though they already held large stakes. I’ve bought Agree Realty A Pref (ADC-A) at an average price of $15.55—opting for the preferred shares rather than the common stock because I’m a bit risk-averse. Plus, interest rates here in Sweden are still low compared to yours, and the USD/SEK exchange rate continues to work in my favor. At the current price—over $16.00—I’m still getting a 6.7% yield, boosted by the currency tailwind, with low risk given the company’s tenant base and low debt levels. It also pays monthly dividends. In other words, this stock is everything that $FBIOP (which I also own) should one day become...
$ADC starter position. Rate environment bad, but I like the portfolio here on the pullback

Adjusted comparable property income grew 4.0%. Portfolio occupancy was 93.8%, with leased space at 96.5% (+110 bps YoY). FY26 Core FFO guidance raised to $7.54–7.58 from $7.48–7.56. 
 
Catalysts in play 
- 117 comparable leases signed across 532K sq ft. 
- New lease rents +14% cash, +25% straight-line. 
- Small-shop leased rate 94.1%, +80 bps YoY. 
- $508M acquisition of The Summit, 870K sq ft retail destination. 
- ~$95M in share buybacks through Oct 9; 59 consecutive years of dividend increases. 
 
Risks to watch 
- Occupancy remained flat at 93.8% YoY despite leasing gains. 
- Comparable property income rose just 2.5% before adjustments. 
- $508M acquisition increases execution and capital needs. 
- Retail tenant weakness could pressure leasing and collections. 
- Higher financing costs could weigh on REIT valuations and investment returns.

However, a Hold-rated analyst warned that core net investment income (NII) has fallen below quarterly dividend payments for two consecutive quarters, raising concerns about dividend sustainability without significant earnings growth. With the October 30 ex-dividend date approaching and third-quarter results due November 9, investors appear cautious. 
 Profit-taking, dividend concerns and macroeconomic uncertainty weighed on the stock, although Raymond James’ upgrade and the strategic review continue to support its longer-term outlook.

$TEN Tanker owner TEN sets a $1.00 January dividend and authorizes up to $150M in buybacks.

🏢 TEN (Tsakos Energy Navigation) is an energy shipping company founded in Bermuda with a pro-forma fleet of 80 tankers and other vessels
💰 The "100% increase" is measured against the $0.50 paid in February 2026, but the $1.00 set for January 2027, about $30M, is the same as the $1.00 TEN paid on July 30, 2026, so the most recent rate holds flat rather than doubling
⚠️ The buyback is only an authorization with no timing, price or share count, it also covers preferred shares, and $150M is about 9% of TEN's roughly $1.61B market value at $53.48 (16:00 ET close, October 23, 2026), so the common share count could shrink by much less than 9%

📅 Next: TEN says the record and payment dates for the January 2027 dividend will be "announced in due course", and any repurchases will depend on market conditions

Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: $UNCY ) has a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of March 25, 2027 for oxylanthanum carbonate (OLC), its investigational oral phosphate binder for the treatment of hyperphosphatemia in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on dialysis, now that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted the company's New Drug Application (NDA) resubmission. The FDA has deemed the resubmission a Class II with a six-month review period from the resubmission date. 
 
Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. is a B2i Digital Featured Company. See the company's in-depth profile at: https://b2idigital.com/unicycive-therapeutics 
 
Under the 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway, the NDA for OLC is supported by clinical, preclinical and Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) data: 
 
• Three clinical studies: a Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers, a bioequivalence study in healthy volunteers, and a tolerability study of OLC in CKD patients on dialysis 
 
• Multiple preclinical studies 
 
• The resubmission includes CMC data from a new third-party drug product manufacturing vendor 
 
Regarding the review, Shalabh Gupta, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Unicycive, stated: "We hope to continue working with the FDA toward potential approval of this important medication to patients with CKD on dialysis who need additional treatment options for managing hyperphosphatemia." 
 
Read the full release: https://ir.unicycive.com/news/detail/128/unicycive-therapeutics-announces-fda-acceptance-of 
 
Unicycive Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing novel treatments for kidney diseases. Unicycive’s lead investigational treatment is oxylanthanum carbonate, a novel phosphate binding agent for the treatment of hyperphosphatemia in patients with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis. Unicycive’s second investigational treatment UNI-494 is intended for the treatment of conditions related to acute kidney injury. It has been granted orphan drug designation (ODD) by the FDA for the prevention of Delayed Graft Function (DGF) in kidney transplant patients and has completed a Phase 1 dose-ranging safety study in healthy volunteers.
